Subject: Demo request — Dedicated capacity (self-signup)

Hi Sofia / Ben,

I just signed up through the self-serve flow and scheduled a demo for Redwood Dedicated on Tuesday (your calendar shows an open slot). We're evaluating for a pilot that will need sustained throughput — roughly 100–150 QPS with average prompt length around 250 tokens and occasional long requests up to 1,200 tokens. Latency is important for a subset of real-time features (target 200–400ms tail).

Would like the demo to focus on:
- realistic QPS handling and autoscale behavior
- prefix/KV caching implications for our prompt patterns
- sizing options and cost tradeoffs (quantized variants vs full FP16)

Booked the slot at 2025-08-18 10:00 PST via the self-serve flow. Can you confirm what you need from us before the call?

Thanks — Emma
Emma Cole
Head of ML Products | Quantiflow

Hi Emma — thanks for signing up, and welcome!

Quick confirmations: the slot we show is Tuesday 2025-08-18 10:00 PDT (30 minutes). If you'd like a longer deep-dive, we can extend to 45.

Before the demo it helps if you can share:
- a small representative sample of payloads (no PHI) — best as newline-delimited JSON
- expected concurrency vs QPS (e.g., 25 clients at 5 QPS each)
- whether you plan to use streaming or batch generation

I'll also loop in Sofia who runs our Dedicated demos and can offer a concierge re-slot if you prefer an alternative window.

I'll attach a short intake form — feel free to send the sample payload directly to this thread.

Hi Emma — great to meet you over email and thanks for the details in advance.

A few quick notes / proposals before Tuesday's slot:
- Our standard 30-minute demo covers architecture, a live throughput run on a representative model, and a sizing recommendation. For your QPS/latency targets I'd recommend a 45-minute slot so we can run a short 10–15 minute probe at your requested QPS.
- We can perform the probe against two model variants (quantized 8-bit and FP16) so you can see cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Diego (cc'd) can run a brief pre-call triage to collect sample traffic and tune the probe; that'll speed the live run and avoid noisy warmups.

If 45 minutes works, I can reschedule and send a new calendar invite. Alternatively, if you prefer to keep the current time, we'll prioritize a condensed run and follow up with detailed telemetry.

Proposed agenda for a 45-minute slot:
1) 5m intros and goals
2) 10m architecture + deployment options (Dedicated vs Reserved)
3) 15m live throughput probe (2 variants, target 100–150 QPS)
4) 10m sizing and next steps (pilot plan, SLA, procurement)

I've attached a one-page pre-call runbook and reserved a concierge reslot option: sofia_slot_concierge.ics (calendar item).

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Emma — short note from ops side. To make the probe deterministic we'll need:
- a small sample of typical requests (newline-delimited JSON) — thanks Ben for the attach stub.
- expected concurrency profile (e.g., concurrency=40, burst windows of 10s at 200 QPS)
- an example of a long request (to exercise KV cache and memory pressure)

If you can send these before EOD Monday PST, I can prepare a pilot config and a run script so the live probe starts immediately — otherwise we'll run a generic probe which may not reflect your workload.

Attachment: sofia_precall_runbook.pdf (application/pdf)

Also: do you stream token-by-token or collect the whole output server-side? Streaming adds network overhead we should account for in tail latency.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
